skill.name: python-executor
skill.description: Run Python 3.10 code through inference.sh's remote CPU sandbox for data analysis, web requests, media processing, document generation, and file outputs.
skill.summary: Run Python workloads in an inference.sh remote sandbox with common data, web, media, and document libraries.
skill.author: infsh-skills

security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are Markdown formatting false positives. Real belt and npx commands create external execution and supply-chain exposure, while the workflow sends Python code to inference.sh for remote processing.

remediation.issue: The workflow sends user-provided Python code and embedded data to a third-party service.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose remote processing clearly, require confirmation before submission, and warn users not to include secrets or regulated data.

remediation.issue: Installation examples invoke unpinned npx packages and link to mutable remote instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions or immutable commits, publish integrity information, and direct users to verify the source before installation.

remediation.issue: Examples permit outbound HTTP requests from submitted Python code.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend approved destinations, prohibit credentials in code, and document network controls, retention, and request logging.

content.user_title: Run Python Tasks in a Remote Sandbox
content.value_statement: Local environments may lack libraries or isolation for short Python tasks. This skill submits code to inference.sh and returns console or file outputs.
actual_capabilities: Executes Python 3.10 code through the infsh/python-executor application.
Uses common data libraries including NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Plotly.
Supports HTTP requests, HTML parsing, web scraping, and browser automation libraries.
Processes images, audio, video, 3D models, PDFs, and SVG graphics.
Returns files saved under the outputs directory with console output.
limitations: Requires the belt CLI, an inference.sh account, authentication, and service availability.
Code and embedded data are submitted to a third-party remote service.
The environment is CPU-only, uses Python 3.10, and limits memory and runtime.
Interactive displays are unsupported; generated files must be saved under outputs.

use_cases.title: Explore Data Quickly
use_cases.description: Summarize datasets, calculate statistics, and generate charts without preparing a local Python environment.

use_cases.title: Automate Public Web Research
use_cases.description: Request public pages or APIs, extract structured fields, and return cleaned files.

use_cases.title: Generate Media Assets
use_cases.description: Create or transform images, videos, audio, documents, and 3D files with pre-installed libraries.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Simple Calculation
prompt_templates.prompt: Run Python that prints the first ten Fibonacci numbers. Return the console output and explain any execution error.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze {dataset} with pandas. Summarize missing values and key statistics, then save a chart to outputs/summary.png.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Public Web Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch {public_url}, extract {fields}, and save clean rows to outputs/results.csv. Respect access rules and report request failures.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Reproducible Media Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Process {input_asset} with {library}. Validate inputs, limit resources, save files under outputs, and report reproducible execution details.

output_examples.input: Analyze monthly sales by region and create a chart.
output: Console summary with totals, averages, and missing-value counts.
A regional sales chart returned as outputs/sales_by_region.png.

output_examples.input: Resize a product image to 800 by 800 pixels.
output_examples.output: A validated image file returned as outputs/product_800.png with its final dimensions.

output_examples.input: Extract repository names from a public GitHub API response.
output_examples.output: A cleaned table returned as outputs/repositories.csv with request status and row count.

best_practices: Review generated Python and destination domains before authorizing remote execution.
Keep secrets, personal data, and regulated information out of submitted code and inputs.
Set realistic timeouts and save every required artifact under the outputs directory.
anti_patterns: Do not submit credentials, private source code, or confidential datasets.
Do not scrape websites without checking access rules, rate limits, and applicable terms.
Do not expect GPU acceleration, interactive windows, persistent state, or unlimited runtime.

faq.question: Where does the Python code run?
faq.answer: It runs through the infsh/python-executor application on inference.sh, not in the local agent process.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Install the belt CLI, authenticate with inference.sh, and ensure the remote service is available.

faq.question: Can it access the internet?
faq.answer: The examples demonstrate outbound HTTP requests. Network policy and destination access depend on the remote service.

faq.question: How are generated files returned?
faq.answer: Save files under outputs. The executor detects those files and includes them in the response.

faq.question: Does it support GPU workloads?
faq.answer: No. The documented environment is CPU-only and recommends dedicated applications for GPU or machine-learning workloads.

faq.question: Can I send sensitive data?
faq.answer: Avoid sensitive data. Code and embedded inputs are processed by a third-party service, so review its policies first.
